title: Cellular Affinity of Particle-Stabilized Emulsion to Boost Antigen Internalization
protocol: Add 0.5 g of polyvinyl alcohol to 120 mL of deionized water at 90 °C.
Stir the mixture until completely dissolved.
Store the PVA solution in a refrigerator after cooling to room temperature.
Mix 100 mg of PLGA with 10 mL of acetone and ethanol (4:1 ratio) to form the oil phase.
Place 20 mL of the PVA aqueous solution under the fume hood.
Magnetically stir the PVA solution at 400 rpm/min.
Add 5 mL of the oil phase into the PVA solution drop by drop using a syringe pump.
Stir the mixture in the fume hood until organic solvents completely evaporate.
Centrifuge the mixture at 15,000 x g after the volatilization of organic solvents (2-3 hours).
Wash the mixture three or more times until the final washing water is clear and transparent.
Re-suspend washed PNPs in 2 mL deionized water.
Freeze the mixture at -80°C for 24 hours.
Subsequently freeze-dry the particles for 48-72 hours.
Add 10 μL of PNPs into 1 mL deionized water to obtain a diluent solution.
Transfer the diluent solution to a DTS1070 cell.
Start the determination procedure in Zeta Size Software to obtain particle size and zeta potential distribution.
Evenly spread 0.1 mL PNPs solution (diluted 40 times) on a tin foil sheet.
Let the water evaporate naturally overnight.
Cut out a small part of the tin foil and secure it on the sample table with conductive tape.
Spray the sample with gold at a current of 10 mA for 120 seconds.
Observe the surface morphology using scanning electron microscopy (SEM).
Reconstitute freeze-dried PNPs in deionized water at a concentration of 4 mg/mL.
Add squalene to the aqueous phase to create an oil-water phase ratio of 1:9.
Prepare PNPE via one-step sonication for 5 minutes at 100 W in a water bath sonicator.
Open the Mastersizer 2000 software and the laser sequentially.
Click on Measure to open the pre-set program and set the sample name.
Start measuring the background of the sample by clicking Start.
Add 1 mL of PNPE to the sample tank using a dropper to measure particle size three times in parallel.
Dilute 20 µL of PNPE in 1 mL of deionized water.
Drop 20 µL of the emulsion on the slide for observation.
Observe the morphology and homogeneity of the emulsion at 40x magnification using optical microscopy.
Obtain photographs of the observed emulsion.
Dissolve 200 µg of ovalbumin (OVA) in 500 mL of deionized water.
Mix OVA solution with 500 mL of PNPE and shake for 1 hour at room temperature.
Centrifuge the mixture at 5000 x g for 20 minutes to remove fluidic antigen.
Determine fluidic antigen concentrations using bicinchoninic acid (BCA) assays.
Divide 6 mL of prepared PNPE into six equal portions.
Store three parts each at 4 °C and 25 °C, respectively.
Dilute 20 µL of stored PNPE into 1 mL of deionized water on day 0, 3, and 6.
Measure the size and zeta potential of diluted PNPE solutions.
Dissolve 500 mg of PLGA in 5 mL of dichloromethane to form the oil phase.
Pour the oil phase into 50 mL of external aqueous phase containing 1.5% PVA.
Homogenize the mixture at 3000 rpm for 1 min using a homogenizer.
Install a 5.2 µm membrane in the membrane tube.
Adjust pressure to 800 kPa and maintain stability.
Open exhaust valve and feed valve, add coarse-emulsions to sample tank.
Close exhaust valve and feed valve, open discharge valve and inlet valve.
Take post-film emulsion from the beaker after process completion.
Repeat the entire membrane emulsification process three times.
Stir pre-double emulsions at room temperature to evaporate dichloromethane.
Wash microspheres using deionized water at 7741 x g for 3 min five times.
Pre-freeze microspheres in a freezer at -80 °C.
Freeze-dry the microspheres to obtain dried microspheres.
Open the Mastersizer 2000 software and laser particle size analyzer in sequence.
Click on Measure to open the pre-set program and set the sample name.
Start measuring the background of the sample by clicking Start.
Add 1 mL of PMPs to the sample adding tank with a dropper.
Measure the particle size of the microparticles three times in parallel using the laser particle size analyzer.
Clean the SiO2 quartz sensor chip by UV-ozone treatment for 10 min.
Rinse the cleaned SiO2 quartz sensor chip twice with 5 mL ethanol (75% v/v).
Dry the SiO2 quartz sensor chip with N2.
Install the empty SiO2 quartz sensor chip into the flow cell.
Turn on the computer and activate temperature control at approximately 1 °C below room temperature.
Click Acquisition in the toolbar, select Setup Measurement to search for octaves of the chip.
Select Start Measurement from the Acquisition button in the toolbar.
Correct the baseline with air when measuring softness.
Stop measurement after baseline is balanced and save file as a blank.
Clean the chip.
Spin coat 10 µg/mL of PNPE on the chip.
Turn on the spin coater and set the operating parameter.
Connect the N2 pipe to the spin coater, adjust the fractionation of the gas cylinder to 0.4 kPa.
Place the clean chip on the suction cup of the spin coater.
Add 100 µL of PNPE dropwise to the center of the SiO2 sensor.
Close the top cover of the spin coater to complete the coating.
Install the PNPE coated chip into the flow cell.
Repeat steps for PNPE coating and save the file as PNPE.
Open both the blank and PNPE files.
Click on the Stitch button to obtain the related data of dissipation (ΔD).
Euthanize the C57BL/6 (female, 6-8 weeks old) mice via CO2 inhalation.
Soak the euthanized mice in ethanol 70% (v/v) for a brief sterilization.
Transfer the mice to a super clean bench after soaking.
Remove leg muscles using stainless-steel scissors to expose the femur and tibia.
Separate the femur and tibia.
Fill a Petri dish with 70% (v/v) ethanol and soak the clean bones in it for 5-10 s to complete external sterilization.
Clean all the bones and place them in a sterile tube with ice around them.
Trim the femur and tibia close to the joint using scissors.
Insert the syringe needle into the bone to flush out the bone marrow into a centrifuge tube using pre-chilled RPMI medium (1640).
Rinse the bone two or three times until it is completely white.
Pipette the bone marrow several times to separate all clumps.
Filter the cells into a 15 mL centrifuge tube using a 40 µm diameter sieve.
Centrifuge at 4 °C and 500 x g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant and add 2 mL of erythrocyte lysate to the sediment for 4 min.
Wash the cells two or three times.
Re-suspend the cells in 2 mL of complete medium (1 % penicillin-streptomycin, 10 % fetal bovine serum, 20 ng/mL of IL-4, and 10 ng/mL of GM-CSF).
Dilute 10 µL of cells into 1 mL of PBS.
Insert the chip of the handheld automated cell counter into the cell dilution for cell counting.
Seed cells at a density of 1 x 10^6 cells/mL into a 10 mm culture dish with complete medium.
Culture the cells in a cell incubator with 5% CO2 at 37 °C.
Change the medium every 2 days.
Transfer the cells to a 50 mL tube on day 7 and centrifuge at 450 x g for 5 min to collect the cells.
Assemble the mini-extruder in sequence as per the manufacturer's instructions.
Check that the syringe housing is not cracked before use.
Ensure all O-rings are in good condition and replace any worn or damaged ones promptly.
Aspirate the BMDCs repeatedly and transfer them to a centrifuge tube.
Harvest cells by centrifugation at 450 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Pressurize cell suspensions through 10 µm, 5 µm, and 1 µm polycarbonate membranes for 30 passes using the mini-extruder.
Centrifuge pooled supernatants for 5 min at 1000 x g and 4 °C to remove cells.
Collect supernatant and centrifuge it at 3000 x g for 5 min at 4 °C to remove remaining cells and cell debris.
Collect the supernatant and centrifuge it at 100,000 x g for 90 min at 4 °C.
Discard supernatant and re-suspend bEVs in 2 mL of HEPES-buffered saline (HBS).
Purify the bEVs via filtration through a 0.45 µm membrane.
Store purified bEVs at −80 °C.
Clean the SiO2 quartz sensor chip using UV-ozone treatment for 10 min.
Rinse the cleaned chip twice with ethanol.
Dry the chip with N2.
Turn on the spin coater by pressing the Power button, then press the Control button to set the coating time and speed.
Place the clean chip on the suction cup of the spin coater.
Add 100 µL of PLL dropwise to the center of the SiO2 sensor.
Close the top cover of the spin coater.
Press the Start button to start coating the sample.
Stop the machine when finished.
Turn off the vacuum pump, turn off the Power and Control buttons.
Remove the PLL-modified SiO2 sensor.
Turn on the computer.
Turn on the electronic unit.
Activate the peristaltic pump.
Activate the temperature control at the bottom right in the software to ensure that the set temperature is approximately 1 °C below room temperature.
Place the PLL-modified SiO2 sensors in the flow cell according to the operating instructions.
Connect the measurement line between the flow cell and flow pump.
Rinse the flow cell with ultrapure water before beginning the experiments.
Click on the Acquisition toolbar and select Setup Measurement.
Search for 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, and 11 octaves of the chip in the channel used.
Click on Start Measurement to allow air to enter the flow module until the air baseline is smooth.
Flow deionized water for 10-15 min to enable solution baseline equilibrium again.
Pump the prepared PNPE solution into the flow module at a flow rate of 50 µL/min to achieve equilibrium adsorption on the SiO2 sensor.
Pump the prepared bEVs solution into the flow module at a flow rate of 50 µL/min to track the process of bEV adhesion to the PNPE surface.
Incubate the BMDCs with 1640 complete media (1% penicillin-streptomycin, 10% fetal bovine serum, 20 ng/mL of IL-4, and 10 ng/mL of GM-CSF) for 7 days.
Seed the BMDCs into small confocal laser dishes at 1 x 10^6 per well overnight at 37 °C in a 5% CO2 incubator.
Mix 0.5 mL of Cy5-labeled OVA (400 µg/mL) with 0.5 mL of PNPE for 1 hour.
Centrifuge at 5000 x g for 20 minutes to remove fluidic antigen.
Resuspend the mixture with 200 μL of deionized water.
Add 10 μL of the formulation (10 μg/mL OVA) into small confocal laser dishes under a super-clean bench.
Co-culture with BMDCs for 6 hours.
Remove the culture fluid from the cells.
Wash the cells twice with pre-warmed phosphate buffered saline (PBS; pH 7.4).
Fix the cells with 4% formaldehyde solution in PBS for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Wash the cells with PBS two or three times at room temperature for 10 minutes each.
Permeabilize the cells with 100 μL of 0.5% Triton X-100 solution for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Wash the cells with PBS two or three times at room temperature for 10 minutes each again.

Cover the cells on the glass-bottomed dish of the small confocal laser dishes with 200 μL of fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC)-conjugated phalloidin working solution and incubate for 30 minutes at room temperature in the dark.
Wash cells with PBS three times for 5 minutes each.
Re-stain nuclei with 200 µL of DAPI solution (100 nM) for approximately 30 seconds.
Switch on the confocal microscope hardware in sequence: laser, confocal unit, microscope, and computer.
Click NIS-Elements AR 5.20.00 software and select Nikon Confocal to enter the testing system.
In the confocal microscope system, turn on FITC, DAPI, and Cy5 channels and adjust HV and offset for each channel.
Select the 100x oil lens and apply a drop of cedar oil on top.
Place small confocal laser dishes containing stained BMDCs on the microscope stage.
Click the Scan button to start scanning.
Under a fluorescence microscope, locate cells of interest by adjusting X-axis, Y-axis, and Z-axis positions.
Tune laser intensity, image size, and other parameters for high-quality confocal images.
Click Capture button to save the captured images.
